summary: Beginner-friendly, local-first retail business intelligence MVP using the exact five-dataset schema, Python ETL/analytics, PostgreSQL, and a Streamlit dashboard. External API source and later hosting target are undecided; no cloud resources or costs in Stage 1.

questions.question: Which language should power the Retail BI app and its ETL/analytics?
questions.rationale: Python is explicitly requested for ETL and is a beginner-friendly fit for the requested analytics and Streamlit dashboard.

options.label: Python
options.description: Use one language for data ingestion, ETL, analysis, machine learning, and the dashboard.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use JavaScript for the application; Python analytics would require a separate service.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Use .NET for the application; Python analytics would require a separate service.

questions.question: Which application framework should be used? You mentioned Dash or Streamlit; the recommended beginner MVP is Streamlit.
questions.rationale: Streamlit keeps the dashboard and Python analytics together for a simpler first release; confirm or enter Dash/another custom framework.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Azure serverless function framework; choose only if that is the intended custom application shape.

questions.question: Review the proposed beginner MVP scope. Which items should be included or deferred: CSV imports for the exact five supplied datasets; data validation and scheduled ETL; PostgreSQL; EDA and dashboard KPIs; K-Means segmentation; sales forecasting; recommendations; anomaly detection; API ingestion; Docker/GitHub; cloud hosting?
questions.answer: Start with CSV import, PostgreSQL, validation, EDA/KPIs, and a Streamlit dashboard; make ML analytics and API ingestion staged milestones. Keep cloud deployment optional and do not provision resources during planning.
questions.rationale: The requested feature set is broad for a beginner. A small end-to-end MVP makes data quality and the supplied schema reliable before adding advanced modeling or external integrations.
questions.recommendedChoice: Start with CSV import, PostgreSQL, validation, EDA/KPIs, and a Streamlit dashboard; make ML analytics and API ingestion staged milestones. Keep cloud deployment optional and do not provision resources during planning.

questions.question: Which external API(s), if any, should the first version ingest, and which deployment target should be documented for later (Azure, AWS, Render, or local-only)? Do not provide credentials or secrets.
questions.answer: Stage 1 is local-first and imports the five supplied CSV datasets. No external API source has been selected; leave API ingestion for a later milestone. Hosting is undecided and deferred; do not provision cloud resources or incur cloud costs now.
questions.rationale: The user selected local-first and has not chosen an API provider or hosting target. CSV-first avoids inventing source fields or adding deployment cost during the MVP.
questions.recommendedChoice: Stage 1 is local-first and imports the five supplied CSV datasets. No external API source has been selected; leave API ingestion for a later milestone. Hosting is undecided and deferred; do not provision cloud resources or incur cloud costs now.

questions.question: Which data stores should the project use?
questions.rationale: PostgreSQL is explicitly requested. PRODUCTS.Image_File remains in the exact schema, but product image files are optional and no Blob/object storage is required for Stage 1.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only in-memory or local application state; cannot satisfy the requested PostgreSQL persistence.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational storage for the five retail datasets and analytical tables.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for product image files referenced by PRODUCTS.Image_File.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application features?
questions.rationale: No sign-in requirement was specified; keep the local beginner MVP simple.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users need to sign in to use application features.

options.label: No
options.description: No user sign-in is required for the initial version.
